**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retire failed intents before allowing another provider**

When a provider returns a definitive decline, handlers such as the event-ticket Datafast path call `recordPaymentFailure`, which marks only the attempt and checkout failed; the synchronization trigger intentionally ignores failures, leaving this newly created canonical intent active. The failed checkout advertises payment methods again, but selecting a different provider creates a different intent key and `createPaymentIntent` rejects it because the first active intent still exists, so legitimate Datafast-to-PayPal (or reverse) fallback cannot proceed even when the provider confirmed no charge. Transition the intent to a terminal state for authoritative no-charge failures before permitting the alternate attempt.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

BLOCKED_OR_AMBIGUOUS: keeping this concern open. recordPaymentFailure receives untyped codes from transport failures, verification mismatches and provider status responses. These do not uniformly establish zero exposure or terminal provider-resource state, so converting all failed attempts into terminal intents would weaken the existing cross-provider double-charge guard. The canonical PaymentFailureConfirmed event exists; the remaining work is a qualified, bound provider-specific no-charge evidence contract plus atomic audited transition/replay tests. No blanket failure synchronization or provider activation was added. Current head 790b239760206cec0c88e2aae29838fa4b4c3fa6 fixes the separate instruction-scope and amount-component environment findings. See docs/payments/component-environment-review-2026-09-16.md for exact code paths, reference limits and the smallest next step.

I researched Datafast’s official documentation rather than relying on generic decline codes. https://developers.datafast.com.ec/index.aspx documents 30-minute checkout expiry, delayed bank responses that may still produce a consumption notice, and verification by payment ID or merchantTransactionId. Its RF/anulación flow reverses an approved transaction; it is not documented as invalidating every possible retry of a hosted checkout. https://datafast.docs.oppwa.com/tutorials/integration-guide permits multiple failed/successful transactions on one checkout, and https://datafast.docs.oppwa.com/reporting-transaction supports querying all transactions for the merchant reference. I could not establish a documented finality/consistency guarantee sufficient for automatic fallback. The decline-based prototype was withdrawn before push; the fail-closed active-intent guard remains. This finding is still blocked, not resolved. Required merchant qualification: Datafast must confirm an authenticated terminal-resource/cancellation condition and how to exclude pending or late authorizations/captures; then validate sandbox traces for delayed response, callback replay and hosted retry, binding all evidence to the configured merchant, environment and immutable checkout. No production payment or credential change was performed, and no secret should be shared in this thread.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Filter advertised routes by the configured merchant account**

After the merchant-boundary fix, a PayPal configuration for merchant B still passes this readiness check when the verified provider account belongs to merchant A, because only the environment is compared. The capability endpoint therefore advertises PayPal and the UI offers checkout, but `validateCanonicalRoute` later rejects every creation attempt due to the merchant mismatch; compare the runtime merchant ID with the activation's `paMerchantRef` before returning the route (and apply the equivalent check to Datafast).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow verification of attempts after checkout expiry**

When a Datafast payment completes near a ticket, course, or Domo hold deadline but its return/status request arrives after expiry, this call rejects before the provider is queried: `createPaymentIntent` validates checkout status and `expires_at` before loading the already-existing idempotent intent. The confirmation handlers deliberately accept expired contexts and contain `payment_after_*_hold_expiry` reconciliation branches, but those branches are now unreachable, leaving a potentially captured payment without the intended reconciliation exception. Permit an existing bound intent/attempt to be reopened for verification while continuing to reject creation of new provider resources after expiry.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Anchor migration introductions in this squash's ancestry**

Fresh evidence for the reviewed squash `335a69a62` is that `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1 for this `introducedBy` SHA and for the entries on lines 542, 547, and 552, because they refer to commits that are descendants rather than ancestors of the squash. `production-release.mjs` performs this check before reading or applying migrations, so releasing this exact commit through the guarded production lane is blocked; point all four entries at ancestors of this commit that contain their respective SQL files.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match bank-transfer availability to the approved merchant**

When an enabled bank-transfer account has any `merchant_account_ref` other than the fixed `tdf-manual-settlement` used by the public booking and service-storefront handlers, this branch still advertises bank transfer as long as instructions exist. Selection then reaches `validateCanonicalRoute`, whose exact merchant comparison rejects every attempt, leaving users with a visible but unusable payment method; require the activation's merchant reference to match the manual-settlement reference before returning this route.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the selected claim through Google signup**

When a signed-in user follows a claim link and then chooses Google in the signup dialog, this redirects them into a claim URL but `LoginPage.handleGoogleCredential` submits only the ID token and consent fields; `completeGoogleLogin` has no claim parameter, so the returned Customer session is sent to generic `/artista/crear` and the selected existing profile is lost. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier claim-flow comment is that the revised `continueClaim` now explicitly enters this signup-only path while the Google branch still cannot transmit `claimArtistId`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Support claims from existing signed-in accounts**

When a signed-in Customer follows a claim link, this forces them into the new-account signup flow, but that flow cannot accept the email already belonging to their account: `runSignupDb` rejects it via `signupEmailExists` before `resolveParty` processes `claimArtistId` (`tdf-hq/src/TDF/ServerAuth.hs:1830-1835`). Consequently, using the profile-associated email fails as an existing signup, while another email fails claim verification, so the customer still cannot claim the selected profile. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier claim-flow finding is that the new forced logout/signup branch preserves the ID but routes it through this incompatible backend contract; this needs an authenticated claim/merge flow rather than another signup.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Send the city filter to the upcoming-events API**

When more than 50 upcoming events exist, this request retrieves only the first 50 globally and the later client-side filter searches that subset. A city whose events fall after that cutoff will therefore show “No hay eventos” even though matching events exist. Include the city in the query key/request (the new endpoint already supports it), rather than treating a limited page as the complete dataset.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Filter public events before applying the result limit**

The database limit is applied before `publicUpcomingEventRow` rejects events by workflow capability, publication metadata, and city. If the first `limit * 3` chronological rows contain enough drafts, private events, or events from other cities, this endpoint returns an underfilled or empty response while eligible later events are silently omitted. Apply these predicates in the query or continue paging until the requested number of qualifying rows is collected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce storefront visibility before returning reviews**

For an anonymous request targeting an inactive marketplace listing or service package, or a deprecated service offering, these branches accept any existing row even though `getMarketplaceItem` rejects inactive listings and `getPackageHandler` returns 404 for inactive packages. Anyone who knows the target UUID can therefore retrieve review bodies and author names for items deliberately removed from the public storefront; apply the corresponding active/deprecation visibility predicates here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require verified email before granting review eligibility**

When a guest marketplace order uses an email whose owner has not registered, an attacker can sign up with that address and become authenticated immediately because `signup` does not confirm email ownership. This email-only predicate then treats the attacker's party as the buyer; the eligibility endpoint enumerates the matching listing and source IDs and permits publishing a “verified” review. The service-package branch repeats the same pattern, so these guest-order sources need a verified-email claim or an order-specific capability rather than `party.primary_email` equality alone.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reuse the public event visibility boundary for reviews**

For a native event with no `external_event_ref`, this condition succeeds regardless of its workflow state, and imported events are checked only for metadata visibility. Consequently, a draft event—or one removed from the public-listable workflow after reviews were created—still exposes review bodies and author names through the anonymous endpoint even though `directory_public_event` would return 404. Check the active `public-listable` capability here as the public event projection does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let users report each failed historical execution**

When a failed or blocked execution is followed by a passing retry before its report is created, the historical-failure gate in `tdf-hq/sql/2026-08-24_studio_audit_historical_failure_gate.sql:27-45` still requires a submitted report linked to that exact earlier execution. This history renders those executions without any report action, while the page’s only “Crear reporte vinculado” button builds its link from `itcLatestExecution`, so the UI can attach a new report only to the later passing run. The plan then remains stuck with `iapFailedWithoutReport > 0` unless an administrator uses the exceptional completion bypass; provide a report link for each historical failed/blocked execution carrying its `itexId`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep missing pilot imports private**

When a draft provider record is absent for two successful runs, `reconcileProviderEvents` replaces its `draft:*` status with plain `missing`. This predicate then returns false, as does the list predicate above, so an ordinary authenticated user can retrieve or list an event that is still `isPublic:false` and was never approved. Track pilot visibility independently or retain the draft marker when reconciling missing records.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep public canonicals visible when one source is draft**

When pilot ingestion merges a new draft provider reference into an existing canonical that still has an active published reference, `draftMayReplaceCanonical` deliberately leaves the public canonical unchanged and `refreshCanonicalVisibility` likewise considers the active non-draft reference public. This any-draft query nevertheless excludes the entire event for non-admin users, while the companion get check returns 404, making an already-approved event disappear until every attached reference loses its draft status. Base the exclusion on the canonical event's effective visibility rather than the presence of any draft source.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
